title: [Bug]: MTP speculative decoding produces repetition collapse with turboquant_* KV cache on sm120 (Qwen3.8-27B hybrid GDN)
body:
### Summary

On an RTX 5090 (sm_120), `Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (`model_type: qwen3_5`, hybrid Gated DeltaNet)
serves cleanly with MTP speculative decoding when the KV cache is `fp8`, and degenerates into
repetition collapse when the KV cache is `turboquant_4bit_nc` or `turboquant_3bit_nc`.

The failure is **silent** — the server boots cleanly, reports a healthy KV pool, answers short
prompts correctly, and only collapses on longer prompts. Output is a single token repeated
~230 times with the answer present in neither `content` nor `reasoning_content`.

### Reproduce

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc --kv-cache-memory-bytes 6442450944 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

Send any prompt of roughly 8k tokens. Short prompts ("What is 2+2?") answer correctly, which
is what makes this easy to miss.

### Results

Held constant: model, MTP K3, `--max-num-seqs 4`. Varied: KV dtype, KV pin, and
`--max-num-batched-tokens`. Metric is the maximum count of a consecutively repeated token in
the response; needle recall on the same prompt.

| KV dtype | pin | mnbt | max consecutive repeat | needle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fp8` | auto | 2048 | **1** | found |
| `turboquant_4bit_nc` | 6 GiB | 512 | 232 | not found |
| `turboquant_4bit_nc` | 6 GiB | 2048 | 230 | not found |
| `turboquant_4bit_nc` | 6 GiB | 4096 | 234 | not found |
| `turboquant_4bit_nc` | 5 GiB | 512 | 224 | not found |
| `turboquant_3bit_nc` | 4 GiB | 512 | 232 | not found |
| `turboquant_3bit_nc` | 5 GiB | 512 | 232 | not found |

12/12 runs with `turboquant_*` KV degenerate; every `fp8` run is clean.

### A second, distinct failure: `num_speculative_tokens: 1` kills the engine

`num_speculative_tokens: 1` with `turboquant_*` KV does not degenerate — it kills the engine
(`HTTP 500`, `EngineDeadError`), 4/4 in earlier runs and 1/1 on a re-run with the traceback
captured:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 314, in get_output
    self.async_copy_ready_event.synchronize()
  File "torch/cuda/streams.py", line 254, in synchronize
    super().synchronize()
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

Three things worth flagging:

- It is **not** the `_continuation_prefill` workspace assertion of #43357. Different failure.
- The engine died on the **first request of the session, which was `"What is 2+2?"`**. Unlike
  the K3 garbling above, the K1 crash needs no long prompt at all.
- The fault surfaces at an async copy-sync point, so this stack is where the error was
  *detected*, not where the kernel faulted. I have not run with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to
  identify the offending kernel — glad to if that is useful.

That run: `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc`, 6 GiB pin, mnbt 2048, `--max-model-len 262144`,
attention block size 3088, `GPU KV cache size: 337,042 tokens`, max concurrency 1.29x.

### Ruled out

- **Stateless-first-chunk recurrent state reuse** (#51562, and the `max_num_batched_tokens`
  below the mamba block size route described in #51483 at `scheduler.py:403-410`). Two
  independent reasons. First, the attention block size here is 3120 and the collapse is
  identical at mnbt 512, 2048 and 4096 — including above the block size, where the aligned-split
  guard holds. Second and more decisively, that defect is **independent of KV cache dtype** —
  it is a GDN recurrent-state path bug. Every `fp8` run here is clean: the `fp8` row above at
  the same mnbt and `--max-num-seqs`, plus a 200-item paired GSM8K run (0 discordant items
  against a no-spec control) and needle recall out to an 85,440-token prompt, all with MTP K3.
  A KV-dtype-independent mechanism cannot explain a failure that appears and disappears with
  KV dtype alone.
- **Prefix caching fast-path losing cached prefix K/V** (#46460). `--enable-prefix-caching` was
  not set in any run here.
- **KV pin size** — reproduced at 4, 5 and 6 GiB.
- **Memory pressure** — the server reports a healthy KV pool (310,789 tokens at the 6 GiB pin)
  and does not OOM.

### Not degenerate: `turboquant_*` KV *without* MTP

`turboquant_4bit_nc` with no `--speculative-config` answers correctly (needle recall passes at
8k, `max consecutive repeat = 1`). So neither MTP alone nor TurboQuant KV alone reproduces
this — only the combination.

### Related open issues

Not duplicates as far as I can tell, but they bound the same path and a maintainer may see a
shared root cause faster than I can:

- **#43357** — nearest in configuration: TurboQuant on SM120 Blackwell, Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4
  hybrid, attention block size 3072, and prompts over ~4096 tokens failing while short prompts
  succeed. I went looking for a shared root cause and **did not find one**: their crash is
  `Workspace is locked ... requires 12.00 MB, current size is 3.06 MB` at
  `turboquant_attn.py:747:_continuation_prefill`, while my K1 crash is an illegal memory access
  detected at an async copy sync, and my K3 case does not crash at all. Listing it so the next
  person does not spend the time twice.
- **#41726** — TurboQuant crash on large chunked continuation prefill, hybrid attention model.
- **#40069** — TurboQuant/HIGGS attention follow-ups tracking issue.

### Possibly relevant

The checkpoint declares `kv_cache_quant_algo: FP8` and ships KV calibration scales;
overriding `--kv-cache-dtype` presumably discards them. The MTP draft head reads the same KV
as the target model, so draft/target divergence would compound. This is a hypothesis, not
something I have isolated.

Worth noting that llama.cpp reportedly runs MTP with `q4_0` KV on this model at 160k context
without degeneration, which suggests the interaction is specific to this path rather than
inherent to MTP with quantized KV.

### Environment

- RTX 5090, sm_120, driver 610.74, CUDA 13.0
- vLLM 0.27.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3, Python 3.12, WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04
- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (compressed-tensors, mixed NVFP4 W4A4 + FP8)
- `Using TURBOQUANT attention backend out of potential backends: ['TURBOQUANT']`
- GDN prefill: `Using Triton/FLA GDN prefill kernel (requested=auto, head_k_dim=128)`

Reproduction scripts and raw per-probe JSON:
https://github.com/Murai-Labs/qwen3.8-27b-rtx5090
